vera_field_note: Ruggedized pelican case, yellow, latched. The sticker is a black circle with a white tree inside it. I don't recognise the logo. Not a brand — something personal, or a group's mark.

yields.content:
--- DAY 1 ---
first program: hello world. felt stupid writing 'hello world' but I did it. It worked. Ran it four times.

--- DAY 8 ---
variables make sense, functions are starting to make sense, loops are the worst thing anyone has ever designed. WHY does it go from i=0 to i<length. Why not i=1 to i=length. Who decided this. I looked it up. Apparently historical reasons. I hate historical reasons.

--- DAY 23 ---
fixed the loop issue (it clicked, I won't explain). Wrote my first thing that was actually useful — a script that renames files in a folder. Ran it on the wrong folder. Renamed three hundred photos with sequential numbers. They're just numbers now. I'm sorry to the photos.

--- DAY 41 ---
Started the greenhouse project. The idea: a small system that reads temperature/humidity sensors and sends an alert if conditions go outside range. For my mother's greenhouse. She doesn't know I'm doing this. It's a surprise.

--- DAY 67 ---
The greenhouse monitor works. It has been running for eleven days without crashing, which I am counting as a success. My mother said 'you made me a robot gardener' and seemed genuinely delighted. She named it Fern. I didn't tell her it's named after a folder called /fern on my hard drive because that's where I kept the project files.

--- DAY 89 ---
I think I want to do more of this. Not as a job. I have a job. But as a — I don't know. A thing I do. It's the only thing I've learned as an adult that felt like something new in my head, like a new room I didn't know was there.

--- DAY 140 ---
Fern is having issues. The sensor keeps reporting impossible temperatures. I think the sensor is bad, not the code. I hope it's the sensor. Haven't told my mother yet.

--- DAY 141 ---
It was the sensor. The code was fine. Replaced the sensor, everything nominal. I was proud of myself for knowing it was the sensor and not the code. That's a new thing too.

--- [ENTRIES MISSING — LATTICE ESTIMATES 60-80 DAYS OF ENTRIES UNRECOVERABLE] ---

--- DAY [CORRUPTED] ---
The greenhouse isn't the point anymore. I've been thinking about the handoff problem — Def mentioned it at the last meeting and I can't stop thinking about it. What happens when one system finishes and another has to pick up. Who ensures the agreement. I wrote some notes. They look like the beginning of something.

--- [FINAL RECOVERABLE ENTRY] ---
Fern is still running. I checked. My mother says it's been very accurate this season. She says Fern is a good name.
yields.vera_note: Lattice recovered most of this. The gap in the middle is real — the tape degraded unevenly. The person who wrote this taught themselves to code in the middle of whatever else was happening, built something for their mother, named a folder Fern and let their mother think she'd named the whole project. The last recoverable entry references 'the handoff problem' and 'Def' — Def also appears in the arbor README from the university lab, credited with notes on the tutorial. I think these are connected. I think the white tree logo was a group, not a brand.
